values.note: $29 a site; one vehicle included (a towed camper or towed car counts with its tow), $8 a night per extra vehicle, which must fit on the site's spur. recreation.gov's 2027 and 2028 tables are also $29.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/narrows-campground-upper-and-lower ('Single Site: $29 per night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234510 (notice 'One vehicle is included in your reservation. Any additional vehicles will be charged $8.00 per vehicle per night') + /rates (2026-2028 Peak Season STANDARD NONELECTRIC 29), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Two sections. Upper Narrows has 7 drive-in sites with back-in parking spurs of 30 to 50 ft (vehicles must fit on the spur; no parking off the road). Lower Narrows is 8 walk-in tent sites reached on foot paths from separate parking. Up to 8 people a site.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/narrows-campground-upper-and-lower ('Each of the seven sites contain a tent pad'; 'This is a walk-in tent camping area with eight sites'; 'RVs, trailers or other vehicles must fit on the parking spur ... The parking length ranges from 30 to 50 feet. Lower Narrows: Parking spaces provided separate from the campsites'; 'A single site may hold up to eight people') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/conditions (Narrows: 15 sites) + catalog 234510 (Upper RV sites all Back-In), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Drinking water until Sept. 30; filling RV tanks at the hydrants is not allowed. Bear lockers at every tent-pad site. Firewood from the host.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/narrows-campground-upper-and-lower ('Vault toilet(s)'; 'Potable water is available at this site') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234510 (notices 'Drinking water is available at the campground until Sept. 30 ... Filling at campground hydrants cross-contaminates the system and is not allowed', 'All campsites with a tent pad have a bear locker'; 'purchased from the host'), read 2026-10-28

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/conditions (Canyon Lakes Ranger District Campground Status: Narrows, Operating Season 'May 15 - Sept 20'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Reserve on recreation.gov up to four days ahead; a reserved site not occupied within 26 hours goes first-come. Sites may be first-come before and after the reservation season (2026: May 15 - Sept 19; 2027: May 14 - Sept 18).

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234510 (rules reservationCutOff 4 days; notices 'Sites may be available on a first-come, first-served basis before and after the reservation season', 'All campsites must be occupied within 26 hours ... If not present the site will be rented by first come first serve basis') + /rates (Peak Season 2026-05-15 to 2026-09-19, 2027-05-14 to 2027-09-18) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/conditions ('Reserve Now'), read 2026-10-28

note: USFS (Arapaho-Roosevelt NF, Canyon Lakes Ranger District) campground in Poudre Canyon on CO-14, ~32 mi northwest of Fort Collins at 6,400 ft, in ponderosa pine and aspen on the Cache la Poudre, Colorado's first National Wild and Scenic River. Rafting, trout fishing and nearby trails (Mt. McConnel, Kreutzer, Young Gulch). Only Upper Narrows takes RVs; Lower Narrows is walk-in tent sites on a slope that drops steeply to the river. --Claude

RV capacity is small: only Upper Narrows' 7 sites take vehicles (catalog lists 6, UPPER 001-006, 001 not reservable); Lower's 8 are walk-in tent sites. recreation.gov's catalog has 14 sites (no UPPER 007); count recorded from FS/ARP as 15.

Length conflict: the FS page and recreation.gov say Upper spurs 'range from 30 to 50 feet' (recorded 50); the catalog gives the six Upper sites 46-55 ft; but the ARP Canyon Lakes status table lists Narrows' 'Max Spur' as 30'. All are well over 23 ft.

Waterfront (stored riverfront) - check, not changed: the Upper Narrows RV sites (catalog points 001-006) line the campground road on a bench between CO-14 and the Poudre; on Esri imagery the river's edge is ~40-50 m west of sites 001-004 across a brushy riparian strip with scattered trees, closer at 004-005 where trees reach the bank. recreation.gov: 'situated ... on the banks of the Cache la Poudre River'. Whether the brush strip counts as an open apron is the re-audit question; the walk-in Lower sites are right by the river but take no RVs.
Pin 40.69129,-105.43214 is at the north end of the Upper loop by the toilet, ~60 m north of site 001 and 197 m from the 14-site centroid (which the Lower tent sites pull south). OK.
